findings.title: Physical and remapped keycode credits lack exact ownership
findings.reproduction: Run proofs/duplicate-count.lua from the macOS driver root: a real key callback plus physical bridge event aggregates keycode 0 and 36 once each for one remapped press. Preserve the passing physical-collision.lua control; explicit global nil suppression makes it lose physical Space.
findings.root_cause: The callback's nil-valued conditional always retains the output keycode. The intended global output-code set cannot distinguish remapped output from ordinary physical input sharing that code; the separate physical ledger has no common output-event identity.
findings.silent_failure: Independent set-membership and aggregation tests do not exercise their combined ownership contract; a duplicate-only fix passes them while losing unjournaled passthrough keys.
findings.regression_test: Require one physical heatmap credit for managed output plus its ledger event, and retain a physical Space credit when Escape emits Space but physical Space is none/none. Use real callback, set builder and aggregation walkers, then verify exact native attribution.
